sylvan esso|hot slob.fact: Hot Slob is Sylvan Esso's first new single since 2022's No Rules Sandy, released in 2026 on their own label, Psychic Hotline. It features drummer TJ Maiani (Weyes Blood, Neneh Cherry) and Jenn Wasner of Wye Oak on extra guitar and vocals.

sylvan esso|concrete glen.fact: Concrete Glen, from Sylvan Esso's 2026 album Ow, samples Sigur Ros' "Svefn-g-englar" - a band singer Amelia Meath has said soundtracked a lot of her childhood.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|crumbli.fact: Crumbling Castle's home album, Polygondwanaland, was released by King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard under an open license with the master tapes posted online for free - inviting fans and small labels to press and remix it however they liked. Hundreds of different fan-made editions exist, including a K.K. Slider-style Animal Crossing tribute pressed on vinyl.

r.e.m.|orange crush.fact: R.E.M.'s Orange Crush is a quietly anti-war song - the title nods to Agent Orange, the defoliant used in the Vietnam War, drawing on singer Michael Stipe's memories of growing up on Army bases where his father served. The subtlety worked almost too well: a British TV host once introduced it on air as "great on a summer's day."

bon iver|holocene.fact: Bon Iver's Holocene takes its title from both the current geological epoch and a bar in Portland, Oregon. Its three verses trace three different moments from Justin Vernon's life in his hometown of Eau Claire, Wisconsin, and the music video was filmed among Iceland's glaciers.

coldplay|don't panic.fact: Don't Panic was the very first song Coldplay ever played live, at their debut gig at The Laurel Tree in Camden, London, in January 1998 - two years before it appeared, reworked with a pump organ, on their debut album Parachutes.

the smiths|still ill.fact: The Smiths' Still Ill got its title from a real conversation - Morrissey's friend, artist Linder Sterling, greeted him at a weekly rooftop-restaurant meetup by asking, "Are you still ill?"

vampire weekend|run.fact: Vampire Weekend's Ezra Koenig has said Run, from 2010's Contra, was written with Bruce Springsteen's Born to Run in mind.

my morning jacket|i will sing you songs.fact: My Morning Jacket recorded It Still Moves, home to the nearly eight-minute I Will Sing You Songs, at Above the Cadillac Studios in rural Shelbyville, Kentucky - with the album's horn parts tracked separately at Memphis's famous Royal Studios.

the strokes|someday.fact: The melody for The Strokes' “Someday” reportedly came to Julian Casablancas while singing in the bathroom, nursing a hangover at drummer Fabrizio Moretti's house - the band built the song around what they heard him singing.

the decemberists|a beginning song.fact: The Decemberists closed their album What a Terrible World, What a Beautiful World with “A Beginning Song” - a hopeful, cathartic track meant to feel like something new being born out of the album's earlier, heavier songs.

alabama shakes|shoegaze.fact: Despite the name, Alabama Shakes' “Shoegaze” isn't about the genre - it's a song about restlessness and loneliness, pivoting on the line “It ain't no fun to be lonely.”

tv on the radio|dlz.fact: TV on the Radio's “DLZ” stands for “Dawn of the Loser,” a phrase from the song's final lines. It wasn't released as a single, but got a big boost in popularity after appearing in a season 2 episode of Breaking Bad.

the cure|catch.fact: The Cure's “Catch” is a light, whimsical love song about a girl from Robert Smith's past whose name he can barely remember - a deliberate 180-degree turn from the album's more aggressive opening track.

kate bush|this woman's work.fact: Kate Bush wrote “This Woman's Work” for the 1988 film She's Having a Baby, matching her lyrics to a dramatic hospital scene the director had already sent her - it's sung from the perspective of a partner realizing how much he loves her.

sault|let me go.fact: SAULT is an anonymous British music collective that avoids media interviews entirely - even their exact lineup is unconfirmed, though producer Dean “Inflo” Josiah Cover (who's worked with Michael Kiwanuka and Little Simz) is rumored to be a member.

khruangbin|time (you and i).fact: Khruangbin's album Mordechai is named after a friend of bassist Laura Lee Ochoa who once encouraged her to jump off a waterfall - the feeling of that leap stuck with her, including on “Time (You and I),” a song about wishing you had more time with the people you love.

broadcast|valerie.fact: Broadcast's “Valerie” takes its name and melody from the 1970 Czech film Valerie and Her Week of Wonders, a major inspiration for the band's dreamy, psychedelic sound.

cherry glazerr|grilled cheese.fact: Cherry Glazerr's “Grilled Cheese” is exactly what it sounds like - a whimsical garage-pop song about grilled cheese sandwiches, written when the band members were still in high school.

boygenius|bite the hand.fact: boygenius wrote “Bite the Hand” about the strange etiquette of fame - not feeling obligated to give fans a piece of yourself just because they bought a ticket, while still making music that's honest.

beabadoobee|beaches.fact: beabadoobee's “Beaches” is a song about self-discovery and not waiting around for the right moment - “Don't wait for the tide, just to dip both your feet in” - built on crunchy guitars that recall Weezer's “Island in the Sun.”

anna burch|tea-soaked letter.fact: In the video for Anna Burch's “Tea-Soaked Letter,” she makes tea, makes toast, and reads tarot cards while waiting to hear from the person she's singing about - a song asking a love interest to actually follow through on better communication.

phoebe bridgers|bobby.fact: Phoebe Bridgers' “Bobby” is her most straightforward love song yet, widely believed to be about her partner Bo Burnham - a warm departure from the melancholic tone of her earlier album Punisher.

hum|why i like the robins.fact: Hum's “Why I Like the Robins” comes from You'd Prefer an Astronaut, an album full of space imagery - this song imagines watching from a window for the robins to return, and seeing the world through a loved one's eyes.

mary in the junkyard|myrtle.fact: Mary in the Junkyard's “Myrtle” is named for a comforting turtle character - “Myrtle told me that I don't need to worry” - part of a concept album imagining the singer's past life as a fisherman.

spoon|got nuffin.fact: Spoon's Britt Daniel described “Got Nuffin” as being about having “nothing to lose but darkness and shadows” - a song about the relief of shaking off negative thoughts.

hoodoo gurus|i want you back.fact: Hoodoo Gurus' “I Want You Back” sounds like a breakup song, but frontman Dave Faulkner wrote it about a former bandmate who quit and was dismissive on the way out - he flipped the anger into a mock “spurned lover” song aimed right at him.

hatchie|quicksand.fact: Hatchie's “Quicksand” catches her in a familiar cycle - feeling ungrateful even when things in her life are, on paper, going well.

weyes blood|movies.fact: Weyes Blood's “Movies” is an ode to cinema as a modern myth-maker - she wants her own life to have the meaning a movie does, even while admitting “the meaning of life doesn't seem to shine like that screen.”

m83|midnight city.fact: M83's “Midnight City” was inspired by late nights watching Downtown Los Angeles come alive, and ends with a now-iconic saxophone solo played by James King of Fitz and the Tantrums.

slow pulp|red car.fact: On Slow Pulp's “Red Car,” a 1996 Mazda becomes a stand-in for the possibility of starting over - part of their album Melodie, about feeling stuck and finding a way to move on.

pavement|unseen power of the picket fenc.fact: Pavement wrote “The Unseen Power of the Picket Fence” as a loving, joke-filled tribute to R.E.M. for a 1994 charity compilation - Stephen Malkmus jokingly name-drops their songs and admits “Time After Time” was his least favorite, which reportedly needled Michael Stipe a little.

the sundays|life goes on.fact: The Sundays' “Life Goes On” opens with “Build me up don't get me down, weather the storm, well, life goes on” - a simple, steady message of resilience from their final album, Static & Silence.

kurt vile|99 bpm.fact: Kurt Vile's “99 BPM” is a nostalgic nod to playing in bands with a friend named Rob back around 2012 - “99 BPM, well, what's that between friends?”

black midi|hogwash and balderdash.fact: black midi's “Hogwash and Balderdash” tells the story of two runaway convicts on the run from the law - who happen to be chickens named Hogwash and Balderdash.

ween|learnin' to love.fact: Ween's “Learnin' to Love” came together after Gene Ween stumbled on a website full of horse-racing betting slang and turned it into a song.

sports team|i'm in love (subaru).fact: Sports Team's “I'm In Love (Subaru)” is a love song about a shiny red Subaru - a stand-in for an idealized, “sorted” adult life that, the song admits, can't actually be bought.

dazy|beat change.fact: Dazy is the one-man project of James Goodson, who started anonymously posting songs on Bandcamp during the pandemic summer of 2020 before it grew into a full band.

talking heads|memories can't wait.fact: David Byrne described Talking Heads' “Memories Can't Wait” as the band's version of a metal song - about memories that keep flooding back no matter how much you try to move on.

vampire weekend|obvious bicycle.fact: Vampire Weekend's “Obvious Bicycle” never actually says the words “obvious” or “bicycle” anywhere in the lyrics - it was just the title Rostam Batmanglij gave the demo the day he wrote it, and it stuck.

angel olsen|all mirrors.fact: Angel Olsen has said “All Mirrors” grew from the idea that “we are all mirrors to and for each other” - a song about how people and memories keep echoing each other over time.

francis of delirium|it's a beautiful lif.fact: Francis of Delirium built “It's a Beautiful Life” out of small real moments - coffee with a pianist about to play a Philip Glass piece, and watching a choir rehearse in a basement - finding beauty alongside everyday loneliness.

swapmeet|bonny.fact: Swapmeet's “Bonny” includes a shoutout to the TV show Malcolm in the Middle - the band has said it made the cut mainly because it fit the syllable count of the line.

future islands|the tower.fact: Future Islands' “The Tower” takes its name and theme from W.B. Yeats' 1928 poem of the same name, about aging and the passage of time, built around the image of a lighthouse cutting through darkness.

bon iver|heavenly father - mediolanum, m.fact: Bon Iver's Justin Vernon wrote “Heavenly Father” for Zach Braff's film Wish I Was Here after talking with his own brother about the film's story of two brothers - it became a song about searching for peace.

black marble|it always comes to me.fact: Black Marble's “It Always Comes to Me” sketches a character who always seems to get away with things, charm or deceit - a modern cousin of The Kinks' “Dedicated Follower of Fashion.”

sharp pins|it's a mod mod world.fact: Sharp Pins is the lo-fi pop project of Chicago musician Kai Slater (also of the band Lifeguard) - “It's a Mod Mod World” is deliberately recorded to sound like catching a British Invasion hit on a handheld AM radio in the 1960s.

sigur ros|inni mer syngur vitleysingur (.fact: Sigur Ros' Icelandic song title “Inní mér syngur vitleysingur” translates to “Within me a lunatic sings.” It's the second track on their 2008 album Með suð í eyrum við spilum endalaust.

beach house|april suzanne (cover version.fact: Beach House's “April Suzanne” is a cover of a 1976 song by Robert Lester Folsom, released as a limited 7″ single (only 1,000 copies worldwide) to celebrate the 50th anniversary of his album Music and Dreams.

mitski|first love-late spring.fact: Mitski has said “First Love / Late Spring” came from falling in love at a moment when she really couldn't afford to. The song describes crying like a “tall child” - looking like an adult while feeling as overwhelmed as a kid.

westside cowboy|coyote.fact: Westside Cowboy is a four-piece band - Jimmy Bradbury, Reuben Haycocks, Aoife Anson O'Connell, and Paddy Murphy - who formed in Manchester in 2023. "Coyote" comes from their debut album, It Goes On, released in August 2026.

lucid express|faux sweetness.fact: Lucid Express is a five-piece dream pop/shoegaze band from Hong Kong. "Faux Sweetness" comes from their second album, Instant Comfort, released via Kanine Records.

black belt eagle scout|soft stud.fact: Black Belt Eagle Scout is the project of Katherine Paul, a Swinomish and Inupiaq musician who has released three albums on Saddle Creek Records. The name came from a conversation with a friend about never having met a black belt who was also an Eagle Scout.

l'rain|elmyra.fact: L'Rain is Brooklyn musician Taja Cheek, who got her start hosting DIY noise shows in her own basement, with acts like TV on the Radio's Kyp Malone stopping by. Her stage name is a tribute to her mother, Lorraine.

this is lorelei|the kid with the crown.fact: This Is Lorelei is a solo alias for Nate Amos, also known as half of the duo Water From Your Eyes. He has released dozens of albums under the name on Bandcamp since 2013.

the passions|i'm in love with a german f.fact: Despite the title, The Passions' "I'm in Love with a German Film Star" isn't really about a German film star - singer Barbara Gogan wrote it about Steve "Roadent" Connelly, a British former roadie for the Clash and Sex Pistols who happened to land a few minor German TV and film roles.

ugly casanova|barnacles.fact: Ugly Casanova was a side project formed by Modest Mouse frontman Isaac Brock in 1997. Brock originally credited the songs to a fictional character, "Edgar E. Graham," a persona he invented so he wouldn't have to do interviews about it.

black flag|gimmie gimmie gimmie.fact: Black Flag started out as Panic in 1976 before renaming due to a conflict with another band using the name. Founder Greg Ginn ran the label SST Records to release their music - a name he'd originally used as a kid selling electronics kits.

cass mccombs|sacred heart.fact: Cass McCombs is one of indie rock's most prolific songwriters, now well past ten albums, and has collaborated with artists including John Cale, Ariel Pink, and The Decemberists. He's also published a poetry collection and made a children's album with a San Francisco schoolteacher.

remember sports|ghost.fact: Remember Sports started out simply as Sports, based in Gambier, Ohio, before renaming in 2017 to avoid confusion with another band called Sports - around the same time they relocated to Philadelphia.

fontaines d.c.|televised mind.fact: Fontaines D.C. formed after its members met studying at Dublin's BIMM Institute, bonding over a shared love of poetry - though the five of them actually grew up in different parts of Ireland (and one in Spain).

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|alien m.fact: Alien Metal comes from PetroDragonic Apocalypse, King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard's 24th studio album - a thrash-metal record released on 13 different vinyl variants, and the first half of a planned "yin and yang" pair with their album The Silver Cord.

the war on drugs|who's that.fact: The War on Drugs was formed by Adam Granduciel and Kurt Vile after the two met in Philadelphia in 2003. Vile left after their debut album to focus on his solo career, but the two never had a falling out and have kept playing on each other's records since.

ty segall|glass.fact: Ty Segall is famously prolific - he's released a new solo album nearly every year since 2008, on top of numerous side projects, EPs, and collaborations.

alex g|mission.fact: Alex G, born Alexander Giannascoli in Havertown, Pennsylvania, built his following recording tapes in his bedroom and posting them to Bandcamp. He briefly performed as "(Sandy) Alex G" after a naming conflict with another artist using the name Alex G.

molly burch / wild nothing|emotion.fact: Wild Nothing is the project of Jack Tatum, who started it in 2009 in Blacksburg, Virginia, after his early demos - including a cover of Kate Bush's "Cloudbusting" - caught the attention of Captured Tracks records.

the national|don't swallow the cap.fact: The National formed in Brooklyn in 1999 after Cincinnati natives Aaron and Bryce Dessner - childhood friends of drummer Bryan Devendorf - were invited to join his band. They later started their own label, Brassland, to release their debut album.

the shins|name for you.fact: The Shins' "Name For You," from their 2017 album Heartworms, was inspired by frontman James Mercer's three daughters - a song of encouragement for young women.

hamilton leithauser + rostam / rostam|a.fact: Hamilton Leithauser (formerly of The Walkmen) and Rostam Batmanglij (formerly of Vampire Weekend) met in 2008 and eventually recorded a full album together, I Had a Dream That You Were Mine, at Rostam's home studio.

typhoon|white liars.fact: Typhoon is led by Kyle Morton and known for its unusually large lineup - the Portland band has featured anywhere from 7 to 17 members on stage.

sufjan stevens|chicago.fact: Sufjan Stevens' "Chicago" comes from his 2005 concept album Illinois and has appeared in the films Little Miss Sunshine and Veronica Mars. He's recorded five different versions of the song over the years.

sufjan stevens|tonya harding.fact: Sufjan Stevens wrote and released "Tonya Harding" to coincide with the 2017 biopic I, Tonya - he'd actually sent the song to the filmmakers first, but they weren't able to find a way to use it.

toro y moi|blessa.fact: Toro y Moi is Chaz Bear, considered one of the pioneers of the chillwave sound alongside artists like Washed Out. He studied graphic design in college and has released seven studio albums that range across wildly different styles.

clairo|amoeba.fact: Clairo (Claire Cottrill) taught herself guitar from YouTube videos at age 13 and was uploading bedroom recordings to Bandcamp and SoundCloud not long after - a self-made bedroom-pop video she posted at 19 made her a star.

broken social scene|can't find my heart.fact: Broken Social Scene is a Toronto musical collective founded by Kevin Drew and Brendan Canning in 1999 that has included anywhere from 6 to 19 members - alumni include Feist and Metric's Emily Haines.

alexalone|electric sickness.fact: alexalone is Austin musician Alex Peterson (who also plays bass for Hovvdy and Lomelda). "Electric Sickness" was actually the very first alexalone song, originally written to score a documentary about Austin BBQ culture and highway gentrification.

big thief|mythological beauty.fact: Big Thief's Adrianne Lenker and Buck Meek met at a show in Boston, then reconnected in Brooklyn as undergrads at Berklee College of Music. They toured as a duo for two years before forming a full band with fellow Berklee grads Max Oleartchik and James Krivchenia in 2015.

deer tick|the dream's in the ditch.fact: Deer Tick got its name from a real deer tick - frontman John McCauley found one on his scalp during a camping trip, panicked for a bit, then decided it made a good band name once he calmed down.

fontaines d.c.|too real.fact: Fontaines D.C.'s "Too Real" comes from their 2018 debut album Dogrel - critics called it the first sign the Dublin band had more range beyond straightforward punk.

stef chura|scream.fact: Stef Chura is a Detroit indie-rock musician known for a distinctive vocal style that swings between a howl and a yodel. She taught herself to home-record after moving to Detroit in 2012 while studying at the College for Creative Studies.

yola|diamond studded shoes.fact: Yola is a Grammy-nominated singer from Bristol, England, who built her career as a U.K. session singer and frontwoman of the band Phantom Limb before going solo. Her debut album, Walk Through Fire, was produced by Dan Auerbach of The Black Keys.

curtis harding|hopeful.fact: Curtis Harding grew up touring with his gospel-singer mother and later became a backup vocalist for Cee-Lo Green, co-writing material and singing on his albums before launching his own soul career.

girl in red|we fell in love in october.fact: Girl in Red is Marie Ulven, a Norwegian musician who taught herself piano, guitar, and production from her bedroom as a teenager. Her breakout song, "I Wanna Be Your Girlfriend," made the New York Times' best songs of 2018 list before she'd even released an album.

unknown mortal orchestra|that life.fact: Unknown Mortal Orchestra is led by Ruban Nielson, whose father was a Maori horn player. Nielson first released UMO music anonymously on Bandcamp in 2010, and the project's self-titled debut album went on to win New Zealand's Taite Music Prize.

lo talker|astral humming.fact: Lo Talker is led by Andrew Shepard, who spent eight years fronting the band Roadkill Ghost Choir - playing every major festival and Late Night with David Letterman - before starting fresh with Lo Talker in 2020, joined by his brother Zach on bass.

tv on the radio|will do.fact: TV on the Radio began in 2001 when neighbors Tunde Adebimpe and Dave Sitek discovered they were both into music and visual art. They made an 18-song demo on 4-track recorders and silk-screened the CD covers by hand to hand out around Brooklyn.

sylvan esso|ferris wheel.fact: Sylvan Esso's "Ferris Wheel," from 2020's Free Love, was the first song the band recorded in the studio they built themselves in the woods near their home in Durham, North Carolina.

jungle|busy earnin'.fact: Jungle is the London duo Josh Lloyd-Watson and Tom McFarland, who have been friends since age nine when they lived next door to each other in Shepherd's Bush. They kept their identities secret when the project started in 2013.

sufjan stevens / angelo de augustine|you.fact: Sufjan Stevens and Angelo De Augustine wrote their collaborative album A Beginner's Mind in a cabin in upstate New York, watching a different movie together every night - each of the album's 14 songs is loosely inspired by one of the films.

neko case|man.fact: Neko Case played in Pacific Northwest punk bands as a teenager before studying art in Vancouver, where she launched a country-leaning solo project. She's also a longtime member of the Canadian band The New Pornographers.

jack white|would you fight for my love?.fact: Before music, Jack White (born John Gillis, the youngest of ten kids) briefly considered the priesthood and ran his own upholstery shop in Detroit. He married drummer Meg White in 1996 and took her last name when they formed The White Stripes.

bachelor|sick of spiraling.fact: Bachelor pairs Melina Duterte (who records bedroom pop as Jay Som) with Ellen Kempner of the band Palehound. The two wrote their first song together in 2018 and recorded their debut album in just two weeks at a house in Topanga, California.

st. vincent|digital witness.fact: Before going solo as St. Vincent, Annie Clark played in the Polyphonic Spree and later in Sufjan Stevens' backing band. She took her stage name partly from the New York hospital where poet Dylan Thomas died, and partly from her great-grandmother's middle name.

barrie|dig.fact: Barrie is led by songwriter Barrie Lindsay, who was discovered almost by accident - a fan who'd heard her music online reached out and helped assemble the rest of the Brooklyn band around her.

beirut|perth.fact: Beirut is essentially one person, Zach Condon, who dropped out of high school in Santa Fe at 17, moved to Paris, and fell in with a group of musicians playing Balkan brass-band music - a sound that became the foundation of his project.

ocs|memory of a cut off head.fact: OCS is one of the many names John Dwyer has recorded under over the years, along with Orinoka Crash Suite, Thee Oh Sees, Oh Sees, and Osees. He's said OCS stood for whatever he decided it meant on any given day.

wolf parade|call it a ritual.fact: Wolf Parade came together in under three weeks - Spencer Krug got a last-minute offer to play a show, recruited guitarist Dan Boeckner, and the two wrote songs together before the band had even rehearsed as a full trio.

madi diaz|nervous.fact: Madi Diaz was homeschooled in rural Pennsylvania, where her woodworker father taught her piano starting at age five. After Berklee and years as a Nashville songwriter, she later joined Harry Styles' touring band on guitar and backing vocals.

illuminati hotties / buck meek|u v v p.fact: illuminati hotties is led by Sarah Tudzin, a Berklee-trained producer and engineer who has worked on records for Coldplay, Lady Gaga, boygenius, and Weyes Blood, plus sound design on the musical Hamilton. She coined the term "tenderpunk" to describe her own band's sound.

arcade fire|month of may.fact: Arcade Fire's Win Butler met founding bandmate Josh Deu in high school at Phillips Exeter Academy. They started the band in Montreal and met Regine Chassagne, now Butler's longtime bandmate, while rehearsing at McGill University.

caveman|work this hard.fact: Caveman frontman Matthew Iwanusa grew up the child of two jazz musicians and sang as a kid in the Metropolitan Opera's Children's Chorus before starting his first band in high school with future Caveman guitarist Jimmy Carbonetti.

valerie june|call me a fool.fact: Valerie June grew up singing in church in Humboldt, Tennessee, and taught herself guitar and banjo. She moved to Memphis at 18 and has since blended blues, folk, soul, and country into her own genre-defying sound - earning praise from Bob Dylan along the way.

grizzly bear|gun-shy.fact: Grizzly Bear started as a solo bedroom project for Ed Droste, recording lo-fi demos on a four-track in his Brooklyn apartment in 2002. The band name was actually a nickname he'd had for an old boyfriend.

sault|free.fact: SAULT is a British collective that has kept its members almost entirely anonymous since 2019 - the only name that reliably shows up in the liner notes is producer Inflo, also known for his work with Michael Kiwanuka and Little Simz.

sincere engineer|tourniquet.fact: Sincere Engineer is Chicago's Deanna Belos, who once aspired to be a dentist before punk rock (and Chicago band Alkaline Trio) took over. She borrowed the band's name from a phrase she heard The Lawrence Arms' Brendan Kelly use in an interview.

skullcrusher|storm in summer.fact: Skullcrusher is Helen Ballentine, who studied graphic design at USC and worked a gallery job before deciding to pursue music full-time and writing her first song, "Places/Plans," in 2019.

hatchie|sugar & spice.fact: Hatchie is Harriette Pilbeam from Brisbane, Australia - "Hatchie" was actually her family nickname growing up. Before going solo she played bass in the bands Go Violets and Babaganouj.

radiohead|if you say the word.fact: Radiohead's members met as students at Abingdon School in Oxfordshire, England, and originally called themselves On a Friday - a nod to the day of the week they rehearsed in the school music room.

alabama shakes|i ain't the same.fact: Alabama Shakes started when Brittany Howard asked classmate Zac Cockrell to write songs together after discovering he played bass in an advanced psychology class at their Athens, Alabama high school.

japanese breakfast|be sweet.fact: Japanese Breakfast's Michelle Zauner is also a bestselling author - her memoir Crying in H Mart topped the New York Times bestseller list and is being adapted into a feature film.

mitski|nobody.fact: Mitski spent her childhood moving between countries including Turkey, China, Malaysia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo because of her father's work with the U.S. State Department, before eventually studying music composition at SUNY Purchase.

andy shauf|the moon.fact: Andy Shauf grew up in Saskatchewan, where his parents ran an electronics and music store - giving him early access to instruments including the clarinet, which is why woodwinds show up so often in his arrangements.

s raekwon|darling.fact: S. Raekwon is Steven Raekwon Reynolds, a producer and multi-instrumentalist from Buffalo, New York, now based in New York City, who writes, produces, and plays nearly every instrument on his own records himself.

tame impala|feels like we only go backwa.fact: Tame Impala is essentially one person, Kevin Parker of Perth, Australia, who started the project as a home-recording effort on Myspace in 2007. He layers his own multi-tracked voice to create the illusion of a full band.

the shivas|sometimes ii.fact: The Shivas formed in Portland, Oregon in 2006 as high-school best friends - brothers Jared and Colby Molyneux plus Eric Shanafelt - and have since toured over 25 countries together.

real estate|ribbon.fact: Real Estate's founding members were childhood friends from Ridgewood, New Jersey who played music together in high school, kept trading songs while away at different colleges, and reunited to form the band after graduating.

turnstile|mystery.fact: Turnstile grew out of Baltimore's hardcore scene in 2010, founded by singer Brendan Yates, who had previously drummed for the band Trapped Under Ice. Their 2025 album Never Enough won two Grammy Awards.

hot chip|night and day.fact: Hot Chip's Alexis Taylor and Joe Goddard met as students at Elliott School in London - Taylor has said going to see Royal Trux play together was the concert that changed everything for him.

michael rault|all alone (on my own).fact: Michael Rault started out self-releasing CD-Rs as a teenager in Edmonton, Alberta, playing in bands with names like the Nightshades before going solo with a sound built on 1960s and 70s psych-pop.

phoebe bridgers|garden song.fact: Alongside her solo work, Phoebe Bridgers has recorded as one-third of boygenius with Julien Baker and Lucy Dacus, and as half of Better Oblivion Community Center with Conor Oberst of Bright Eyes. She's won four Grammy Awards from eleven nominations.

yves tumor|noid.fact: Yves Tumor (Sean Bowie) is a self-taught musician who plays drums, bass, guitar, and keyboards. After moving to Los Angeles, they joined rapper Mykki Blanco's music group and spent over two years touring Europe and Asia with them.

lcd soundsystem|i can change.fact: LCD Soundsystem's James Murphy co-founded the influential label DFA Records in 2001 - the initials jokingly stood for "Death From Above" - before launching LCD Soundsystem itself the following year.

hovvdy|around again.fact: Hovvdy's Charlie Martin and Will Taylor met by chance at a Colorado Rockies baseball game in Denver in 2014, where both happened to be touring with separate bands - they bonded over songwriting and started Hovvdy together in Austin.

beach house|zebra.fact: Beach House's Victoria Legrand and Alex Scally met in Baltimore's indie scene and first played together in a band called Daggerhearts before forming Beach House in 2004. Their song "Apple Orchard" being featured on Pitchfork's Infinite Mixtape gave them their first big break.

yo la tengo|i'll be around.fact: Yo La Tengo's Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley are a married couple - they met at a Feelies concert in Hoboken, New Jersey in 1980, married in 1987, and have played together in the band ever since.

the xx|say something loving.fact: Two members of The xx, Romy Madley Croft and Oliver Sim, actually met in preschool at age three, growing up in the same London suburb. They reconnected years later at secondary school to start the band.

my morning jacket|love love love.fact: My Morning Jacket's Jim James recorded vocals for their early album At Dawn inside an abandoned grain silo on his family's Kentucky soybean farm, drawn to its natural reverb.

spud cannon|juno.fact: Spud Cannon formed at Vassar College in 2016 and went through several other names - including The Black Jeans and Paper Dots - before settling on Spud Cannon. Their album Squeeze climbed to No. 3 on the College Radio Top 200.

the killers|in the car outside.fact: The Killers' Brandon Flowers found guitarist Dave Keuning through a classified ad in a Las Vegas newspaper after being fired from his own first band. The two bonded over shared influences and started writing together right away.

grimes|california.fact: Grimes (Claire Boucher) moved from Vancouver to Montreal at 18 to study neuroscience and electroacoustics at McGill University, with a minor in Russian literature, before getting pulled into the city's underground music scene.

snail mail|valentine.fact: Snail Mail's Lindsey Jordan started classical guitar lessons at age five and was writing her own songs by 12. She first performed as Snail Mail at just 15 years old and was quickly hailed as a guitar prodigy.

big red machine / taylor swift|renegade.fact: Big Red Machine pairs Justin Vernon of Bon Iver with Aaron Dessner of The National - it started as a demo Dessner sent Vernon for a compilation album, which grew into a full collaborative project with dozens of contributing musicians, including Taylor Swift on "Renegade."

bon iver|22 (over s88n).fact: On Bon Iver's album 22, A Million, Justin Vernon said the number 22 represents himself, something tangible, while "a million" stands for something abstract and infinite - each song's odd, symbol-filled title works the same way.

car seat headrest|stop smoking.fact: Car Seat Headrest gets its name from Will Toledo's early recording setup - at 17, he'd record vocals sitting in his family's parked car for privacy and soundproofing. He self-released 12 albums on Bandcamp before signing to Matador Records.

the black keys|everlasting light.fact: The Black Keys' Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney grew up a few houses apart in Akron, Ohio, and first met around age nine - though it was their older brothers who eventually pushed the two to start jamming together in Carney's basement.

parcels|comingback.fact: All five members of Parcels grew up together in Byron Bay, Australia, and formed the band in their final year of high school. After moving to Berlin, they played a 2016 Paris show that happened to have Daft Punk in the crowd - leading to a co-writing credit on the duo's single "Overnight."

the new pornographers|falling down the s.fact: The New Pornographers are a Vancouver "supergroup" of songwriters from other projects - members include alt-country star Neko Case and Dan Bejar, who also records as Destroyer.

sigur ros|ísjaki.fact: Sigur Ros formed in Reykjavik in 1994 and is named after singer Jonsi Birgisson's baby sister, Sigurros Elin. Jonsi is known for playing his guitar with a cello bow, a technique that helped define the band's ethereal sound.

radiohead|jigsaw falling into place.fact: Radiohead released In Rainbows in 2007 letting fans pay whatever they wanted for it, with no minimum price. The average payment ended up around .26 - and the album still went on to debut at No. 1 once it got a physical release.

radiohead|everything in its right place.fact: Radiohead's "Everything in Its Right Place" started as a piano song, but early full-band arrangements kept falling flat - the breakthrough came when Thom Yorke and producer Nigel Godrich took it apart and rebuilt the piano chords as synth tones instead.

hand habits|aquamarine.fact: Hand Habits is guitarist Meg Duffy, who started on drums in 5th grade before switching to guitar at 17. Beyond their own project, Duffy has toured and recorded with Kevin Morby and Perfume Genius, and played on records by Weyes Blood and Hurray for the Riff Raff.

mgmt|i found a whistle.fact: MGMT's Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser met as freshmen at Wesleyan University and made their first recordings in Goldwasser's dorm room. The band was originally called The Management, later shortened to MGMT after learning another band already had that name.

vampire weekend|harmony hall.fact: Vampire Weekend's "Harmony Hall" was the lead single from 2019's Father of the Bride, arriving after a six-year gap between albums - its lyrics even interpolate a line from their earlier song "Finger Back."

american wrestlers|holy.fact: American Wrestlers is Gary McClure, a Scottish musician who moved to St. Louis, Missouri to marry his girlfriend. He started the project using her guitar and keyboard plus a bass and 8-track recorder he bought at a pawn shop, posting the results anonymously to Bandcamp.

torres|hand in the air.fact: Torres is Mackenzie Scott, who took her stage name from her grandfather's surname. She recorded her 2013 debut album in just five days at the Nashville home studio of "swamp rock" legend Tony Joe White while still a student at Belmont University.

lower dens|young republicans.fact: Lower Dens' Jana Hunter formed the band in 2010 after realizing what she'd actually grown tired of wasn't touring - it was performing her old solo material live. Putting together a backing band for one last tour led straight into starting Lower Dens.

tv on the radio|happy idiot.fact: "Happy Idiot" was the first single from TV on the Radio's Seeds, the band's first album after the 2011 loss of longtime bassist Gerard Smith. It was recorded at guitarist Dave Sitek's home studio in Los Angeles, with Sitek producing.

thee oh sees|crushed grass.fact: John Dwyer of Thee Oh Sees is remarkably prolific, releasing music under the band's various names at a rate of roughly an album a year for two decades. He also co-runs Castle Face Records, a label with nearly 200 releases that's also home to Ty Segall.

scruffpuppy|assignment.fact: Scruffpuppy is Jodi Shubert, who grew up in Paris, Texas before moving to Wisconsin. She built a following posting lo-fi bedroom covers on YouTube before self-releasing her own albums and eventually signing to Phoebe Bridgers' label, Saddest Factory Records.

fleet foxes|tiger mountain peasant song.fact: Fleet Foxes' 2008 debut is full of layered vocal harmonies, but "Tiger Mountain Peasant Song" strips all that away for a solo showcase of frontman Robin Pecknold over a single spare guitar part.

casper skulls|lingua franca.fact: Casper Skulls formed in 2015 when Toronto-based musicians (and partners) Neil Bednis and Melanie St-Pierre started writing together. "Lingua Franca" itself earned the band a SOCAN Songwriting Prize nomination in 2018.

parquet courts|walking at a downtown pac.fact: Parquet Courts' Andrew Savage and Austin Brown met at the University of North Texas in a club called Knights of the Round Turntable, where members shared and listened to new records together.

kings of convenience|fever.fact: Kings of Convenience's Erlend Oye and Eirik Boe met as kids in the same Bergen, Norway classroom - their first-ever performance together was a comedic rap about one of their teachers.

elbow|my sad captains.fact: Elbow's members met in 1990 at a college near Bury, Greater Manchester, and played together for years under the name Mr. Soft (borrowed from a Cockney Rebel song) before settling on Elbow in 1997.

andrew bird|a nervous tic motion of the.fact: Andrew Bird picked up the violin at age four and studied it formally at Northwestern University. His live shows are built entirely in real time with loop pedals - he'll pluck out a violin intro, loop it, bow the strings for another layer, whistle a melody, then pick up a guitar, building each song piece by piece on stage.

the war on drugs|i don't live here anymo.fact: The War on Drugs' Adam Granduciel has said the title I Don't Live Here Anymore describes a feeling more than a place - "you know exactly what you're not, but that doesn't mean you know where you're going." The record was written as he was becoming a father.

spirit of the beehive|the server is imme.fact: Spirit of the Beehive formed in Philadelphia in 2014 and took their name from a 1973 Spanish film of the same title. The band has restlessly reinvented its sound with nearly every release, from shoegaze to glitchy, vaporwave-tinged electronics.

crying|vacation.fact: Crying formed at SUNY Purchase in 2013 and originally built their sound around a Game Boy, blending chiptune bleeps with pop hooks before evolving into more classic-rock-influenced territory on later releases.

cat power|manhattan.fact: Cat Power is Chan Marshall, who named the project after a trucker cap reading "Cat Diesel Power" that she spotted while working at a pizza shop. She was discovered opening for Liz Phair in 1994 by Sonic Youth's Steve Shelley, and has since influenced artists like Mitski, Snail Mail, and Angel Olsen.

lucy dacus|hot & heavy.fact: Lucy Dacus grew up in the Richmond, Virginia area, the daughter of a music teacher, and was writing her own songs by age eight. She later formed boygenius with fellow songwriters Phoebe Bridgers and Julien Baker, and the trio won two Grammys for their debut album.

the magnetic fields|'81: how to play the.fact: The Magnetic Fields is largely the vision of songwriter Stephin Merritt, who started the project as essentially a one-man show before childhood friend Claudia Gonson joined as drummer and manager. Their best-known work, 69 Love Songs, is a three-disc, 69-track concept album spanning genres from country to synth-pop.

angel olsen|safety dance.fact: Angel Olsen moved from St. Louis to Chicago at 20 and fell in with the city's DIY music scene. A friend passed her demos along to folk musician Bonnie "Prince" Billy (Will Oldham), who invited her to sing backing vocals on two of his albums before she launched her solo career.

the decemberists|january hymn.fact: The Decemberists take their name from the Decembrist revolt, an 1825 uprising in Imperial Russia - frontman Colin Meloy has said the name was also meant to capture the "drama and melancholy" of the month of December.

current joys|amateur.fact: Current Joys is Nick Rattigan, who also drums and sings for the band Surf Curse. He borrowed the name Current Joys from a song by folk musician Liam the Younger after recording under a couple of other names first.

pure bathing culture|pray for rain.fact: Pure Bathing Culture's Sarah Versprille and Daniel Hindman met in college in New Jersey and started writing songs together while living in Brooklyn, before relocating to Portland, Oregon in 2011, where the band came together.

spelling|always.fact: SPELLLING is Oakland musician Chrystia "Tia" Cabral, who started out focused on visual art before turning to music in 2015 - building her sound from looping pedals, synths, drums, and guitar. Her catalog has grown steadily more ambitious, from her self-released 2017 debut to 2021's orchestrated The Turning Wheel.

andrew bird|sisyphus.fact: Andrew Bird's "Sisyphus," from 2019's My Finest Work Yet, retells the Greek myth of the trickster condemned to push a boulder uphill forever - midway through the song, the music itself pauses on the lyric "paused," a deliberate fermata built right into the arrangement.

chubby and the gang|i hate the radio.fact: Chubby and the Gang formed in 2019 out of London's hardcore punk scene - frontman Charlie "Chubby" Manning-Walker had been playing in bands like Violent Reaction since his teens before teaming up with members of Brighton's Vile Spirit and Gutter Knife. Their debut album, Speed Kills, was produced by Jonah Falco of Fucked Up.

wild nothing|tv queen.fact: Wild Nothing's "TV Queen," from 2016's Life of Pause, was recorded across sessions in Los Angeles and Stockholm with producer Thom Monahan - Peter Bjorn and John's John Eriksson guested on drums and marimba.

silbo gomero|bellcast.fact: Silbo Gomero, the Chicago/Fort Wayne electronic duo behind "Bellcast," shares its name with a real whistled language once used by shepherds on La Gomera in the Canary Islands to communicate across the island's deep ravines.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|yours.fact: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's "Yours," written by frontman Stu Mackenzie, opens 2021's Butterfly 3000 - a bright synth-pop turn for the famously genre-hopping band, built around the simple idea of finding comfort and security in another person.

sylvan esso|runaway.fact: Sylvan Esso's "Runaway," from 2020's Free Love, pairs Amelia Meath's bright, elated vocal with skittering, 8-bit-style synths from producer Nick Sanborn - the pair write and record together as a duo out of their own studio in Durham, North Carolina.

wilder|hang up.fact: Wilder is the long-running project of Long Beach, California musicians Stephen Ramos and Nick Sturz, who had already spent a decade writing, touring, and recording together in other bands before releasing "Hang Up."

big thief|paul.fact: Big Thief's "Paul," from their 2016 debut album Masterpiece, reads like a song about an ex-lover, but Adrianne Lenker has said it's really about reconciling two sides of her own personality - she described the lyrics as arriving almost like a future version of herself narrating "the whole story."

sufjan stevens / angelo de augustine|fic.fact: Sufjan Stevens and Angelo De Augustine's "Fictional California," from 2021's A Beginner's Mind, was loosely inspired by the movie Bring It On - De Augustine has said California itself can feel almost fictional, "like a fantasy movie where everyone has their own character and role they feel expected to play." The whole album grew out of the two watching a different film together each night while writing songs in an upstate New York cabin.

arcade fire|ready to start.fact: Arcade Fire's "Ready to Start" was the very first song written for 2010's The Suburbs, which went on to win Album of the Year at the Grammys - the band played it live at the ceremony immediately after taking home the award.

sault|don't waste my time.fact: SAULT's "Don't Waste My Time" comes from 5, the anonymous British collective's 2019 debut album - the opening chapter in a remarkably prolific run of celebrated releases the group has kept up without ever doing press or revealing its full lineup.

curtis harding|i won't let you down.fact: Curtis Harding's "I Won't Let You Down" comes from his 2022 album If Words Were Flowers, built around a classic soul groove layered with horns, background singers, and modern psychedelic touches.

skullcrusher|song for nick drake.fact: Skullcrusher's "Song for Nick Drake" is Helen Ballentine's homage to the late folk singer's music - the song traces specific memories, like train rides and long walks, tied to listening to his songs. It followed her debut EP and a b-side cover of Radiohead's "Lift."

strand of oaks|shut in.fact: Strand of Oaks' "Shut In" comes from 2014's HEAL, an album singer-songwriter Timothy Showalter wrote in a three-week creative burst during a period of personal turmoil - he came out of it with some 30 songs, trimmed down to the ten that made the record, with mixing by John Congleton.

unknown mortal orchestra|hunnybee.fact: Unknown Mortal Orchestra's "Hunnybee," from 2018's Sex & Food, began during a monsoon in Vietnam - frontman Ruben Nielson wrote it as a kind of time-capsule message of advice for his young daughter, Iris, to look back on someday.

the murlocs|bittersweet demons.fact: The Murlocs were formed in 2010 by Ambrose Kenny-Smith, who also sings and plays harmonica in King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard - he'd known Murlocs drummer Matt Blach since primary school, though the two didn't start playing together until Kenny-Smith met guitarist Cal Shortal at a house party. "Bittersweet Demons," the title track from their 2021 album, gave the band their first top-ten entry on Australia's ARIA charts.

mogwai|ritchie sacramento.fact: Mogwai's "Ritchie Sacramento" got its odd title from a friend of the band's mishearing the name of composer Ryuichi Sakamoto. It's also the only track with clean vocals on the mostly-instrumental As the Love Continues, which became the band's first-ever UK #1 album some 25 years after their debut single.

tame impala|reality in motion.fact: Tame Impala's "Reality in Motion" closes out 2015's Currents - one of the few moments on that mostly synth-driven album where Kevin Parker reaches back for his older, guitar-driven sound, with erratic rhythm changes mirroring the song's racing, overdriven feeling.

caribou|you can do it.fact: Caribou's "You Can Do It" is built around a chopped-up, delirious vocal sample of its own title - Dan Snaith released it as a surprise one-off single after 2020's Suddenly, paired with a music video that's just dogs happily chasing frisbees through scenic landscapes. It earned a Grammy nomination for Best Dance Recording.

chairlift|i belong in your arms.fact: Chairlift's "I Belong in Your Arms," from 2012's Something, was written by the duo of Caroline Polachek and Patrick Wimberly, who formed the band in Boulder, Colorado in 2005. Decades later, the '80s-influenced synthpop song found a whole new audience soundtracking the closing scene of the TV series Heartstopper.

pom pom squad|head cheerleader.fact: Pom Pom Squad's "Head Cheerleader," from 2021's Death of a Cheerleader, was co-produced by frontwoman Mia Berrin and Sarah Tudzin of illuminati hotties - the album blends riot-grrrl and Kerplunk-era Green Day influences with Motown and old Hollywood glamour.

sharon van etten|seventeen.fact: Sharon Van Etten's "Seventeen," from 2019's Remind Me Tomorrow, is an ode to New York City that started out as a slow, Lucinda Williams-style dirge before turning into a Springsteen-esque anthem. Its music video pairs Van Etten with an actress playing a teenage version of her, retracing her old haunts around the city.

cate le bon|home to you.fact: Cate Le Bon's "Home to You," a 2019 single from her album Reward, came out of a year she spent almost entirely off the road, taking a daily furniture-making course in England's Lake District - by day she learned dovetail joints, and by night she wrote the songs that became the album.

deafheaven|great mass of color.fact: Deafheaven's "Great Mass of Color" introduced 2021's Infinite Granite, an album that traded much of the band's earlier black-metal roar for shoegaze and clean vocals - it was produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen (M83, Paramore, Wolf Alice) and mixed by Darrell Thorp, known for his work with Radiohead and Beck.

viagra boys|ain't nice.fact: Viagra Boys' "Ain't Nice" introduced 2021's Welfare Jazz, the Stockholm punk band's second album - produced by the same team behind classic records from The Hives and The Knife, with additional work from Matt Sweeney (Chavez) and the Raisen brothers, who've also produced for Yves Tumor and Kim Gordon.

jo passed|sold.fact: Jo Passed's "Sold" comes from Their Prime, the Vancouver band's 2018 debut full-length for Sub Pop. The project started as just singer Jo Hirabayashi and drummer Mac Lawrie, who moved to Montreal together and toured across the continent before growing into a full band.

julien baker|ringside.fact: Julien Baker's "Ringside," from 2021's Little Oblivions, comes from the first Julien Baker album built around a full-band sound - she produced it herself and played nearly every instrument, with boygenius bandmates Phoebe Bridgers and Lucy Dacus contributing backing vocals.

low|disappearing.fact: Low's "Disappearing" comes from 2021's Hey What, the Minnesota duo's only album recorded just as a two-piece - Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker's two vocals sit inside waves of distorted, roaring noise, produced by BJ Burton, who also helped shape Bon Iver's 22, A Million.

deerhunter|memory boy.fact: Deerhunter's "Memory Boy" comes from 2010's Halcyon Digest, an album frontman Bradford Cox has described as noise rock colliding with baroque pop - it was released as a single paired with "Nosebleed" the following year.

baio|sister of pearl.fact: Chris Baio, bassist of Vampire Weekend, wrote "Sister of Pearl" as a Bowie- and Bryan Ferry-referencing throwback pop song for The Names, his 2015 solo debut - its message, as he put it, boils down to "be who you want to be."

wild pink|pacific city.fact: Wild Pink's "Pacific City," from 2021's A Billion Little Lights, is named for the small town on the Oregon coast - frontman John Ross wrote it while watching the movie Heat, and it features the band's first-ever saxophone solo, played by Stephen Chen of San Fermin.

real estate|talking backwards.fact: Real Estate's "Talking Backwards," the lead single from 2014's Atlas, was recorded at New York's Magic Shop studio with producer Tom Schick - Pitchfork named it a Best New Track, and NPR and Rolling Stone both later called it one of the best songs of that year.

wye oak|its way with me.fact: Wye Oak's "Its Way With Me," written by the songwriting duo of Andy Stack and Jenn Wasner, is about learning to feel at peace amid change and things beyond your control - a theme the Baltimore duo has returned to since reinventing their sound around Wasner's bass playing on 2014's Shriek.

car seat headrest|maud gone.fact: Car Seat Headrest's "Maud Gone," from 2015's Teens of Style, is written from the perspective of Irish poet W.B. Yeats about his real-life muse, Maud Gonne - a revolutionary he was infatuated with for years and proposed to five times, always unsuccessfully.

mac demarco|ode to viceroy.fact: Mac DeMarco recorded his 2012 album 2, home to "Ode to Viceroy," entirely in his Mile End, Montreal apartment - by his own account, wearing nothing but his underwear the whole time.

phoebe bridgers|i know the end.fact: Phoebe Bridgers' "I Know the End" closes out 2020's Punisher with a three-part build that ends in a cathartic scream - when she performed it on Saturday Night Live in February 2021, she capped the segment by smashing her guitar against a studio monitor.

gruff rhys|loan your loneliness.fact: Gruff Rhys' "Loan Your Loneliness" was the lead single from 2021's Seeking New Gods, his seventh solo album - a record loosely inspired by the imagined history of Mount Paektu, the volcano straddling the border of North Korea and China.

colleen green|it's nice to be nice.fact: Colleen Green's "It's Nice to Be Nice," from 2021's Cool, is a plea to hold onto kindness even when it's easier not to - Green co-produced the album with Gordon Raphael, the producer best known for shaping The Strokes' early sound on Is This It.

destroyer|savage night at the opera.fact: Destroyer's "Savage Night at the Opera," from 2011's Kaputt, rides the same smooth, sax-and-synth "yacht rock" sound Dan Bejar built across the whole album while obsessing over Roxy Music's Avalon - Kaputt went on to become the unexpected commercial peak of his career.

big red machine|mimi (feat. ilsey).fact: Big Red Machine's "Mimi," featuring songwriter Ilsey Juber (who's written for Beyonce, Shawn Mendes, and Lykke Li), takes its title from Aaron Dessner's youngest daughter - he wrote it while thinking about how grateful he was for his kids during a hard stretch.

illuminati hotties|threatening each othe.fact: illuminati hotties' "Threatening Each Other re: Capitalism" is a more melancholy detour on 2021's Let Me Do One More from bandleader and producer Sarah Tudzin, who's also produced records for Pom Pom Squad, boygenius, and Weyes Blood.

dirty projectors|that's a lifestyle.fact: Dirty Projectors' "That's a Lifestyle," from 2018's Lamp Lit Prose, features guest vocals from HAIM - the song's sound recalls the band's earlier Bitte Orca era, with acoustic 12-string guitar bursting into distorted electric squalls.

beirut|postcards from italy.fact: Beirut's "Postcards from Italy" comes from 2006's Gulag Orkestar, recorded mostly alone in his childhood bedroom by a teenage Zach Condon before he finished the album in New Mexico with Jeremy Barnes of Neutral Milk Hotel and A Hawk and a Hacksaw.

the national|apartment story.fact: The National's "Apartment Story," from 2007's Boxer, was written by Matt Berninger and Aaron Dessner and produced by longtime collaborator Peter Katis - it became the album's second single after the band debuted it that same year on The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson.

jose gonzalez|swing.fact: Jose Gonzalez's "Swing," from 2021's Local Valley - his first new album in six years - blends West African highlife guitar lines with Caribbean rhythms into a song about body positivity, built around the simple message that it's okay to move however you want, wherever you are.

vampire weekend|oxford comma.fact: Vampire Weekend's "Oxford Comma" name-checks Lil Jon in a song about grammar and not caring too much about the rules - Lil Jon was apparently flattered enough by the shoutout to send the band a case of his own Crunk Juice energy drink, and a real friendship followed.

the new pornographers|you'll need a new.fact: The New Pornographers' "You'll Need a New Backseat Driver" comes from 2019's In the Morse Code of Brake Lights, written entirely by A.C. Newman - he didn't set out to make a concept album, but noticed partway through that the songs kept circling back to cars and driving, which became the record's throughline.

my morning jacket|the day is coming.fact: My Morning Jacket's "The Day Is Coming" comes from 2011's Circuital, the band's sixth studio album - a deliberate return to warmer, more live-sounding production after the heavily synthesized, dub-and-reggae-tinged detour of 2005's Z.

angel olsen|intern.fact: Angel Olsen's "Intern" opens 2016's My Woman with a total left turn into synthpop - she's described it as something of a joke aimed at expectations, made with friends who work in synth music because she wanted to do "something sarcastic" after her earlier, more traditional records.

angel olsen|sister.fact: Angel Olsen's "Sister," from 2016's My Woman, stretches out past the eight-minute mark as the full band improvises and builds - one of several ways the album's back half deliberately loosens up after the tighter, poppier songs that open it.

ducks ltd.|under the rolling moon.fact: Ducks Ltd.'s "Under the Rolling Moon," from their 2021 debut album Modern Fiction, features backing harmonies from members of the New Zealand band The Beths - bandmember Tom McGreevy has said the song is about trying to be there for a friend going through a hard time.

woods|shining.fact: Woods' "Shining," from 2014's With Light and With Love, packs a lot of sound into just two minutes - Pitchfork described its lush arrangement as showing off "darker shades of American Beauty," a nod to the Grateful Dead's classic 1970 album.

st. vincent|prince johnny.fact: St. Vincent's "Prince Johnny," from her self-titled 2014 album, is a tribute to a real friend of Annie Clark's - a portrait of the kind of New York City nightlife scene where people who fled their hometowns come to reinvent themselves.

cheekface|we need a bigger dumpster.fact: Cheekface's "We Need a Bigger Dumpster" pairs chipper pop-rock with singer Greg Katz's deadpan, non-sequitur-filled delivery - the Los Angeles trio (Katz, bassist Amanda Tannen, and drummer Mark "Echo" Edwards) built its whole style around that mismatch between upbeat music and wry, anxious lyrics.

king gizzard & the lizard wizard|cyboogi.fact: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's "Cyboogie" appears on 2021's Butterfly 3000, an album that began as loops of arpeggiated modular synthesizers before being reworked into dream-pop songs - it was also the first King Gizzard album released on the band's own label, KGLW, rather than through Flightless Records.

sleigh bells|locust laced.fact: Sleigh Bells' "Locust Laced" comes from 2021's Texis, the duo's fifth album and first in five years - its music video imagines the band performing on an old-timey country TV program that spirals into complete chaos.

islands|(we like to) do it with the ligh.fact: Islands' "(We Like To) Do It With the Lights On" comes from 2021's Islomania, the band's first album in five years - frontman Nick Thorburn has said the tongue-in-cheek title started as a throwaway joke, and that he built the song's melody on top of the groove first, a new approach for him on this record.

shannon and the clams|the boy.fact: Shannon and the Clams' "The Boy," the lead single from 2018's Onion, was recorded in just ten days at Dan Auerbach's Easy Eye Sound studio in Nashville - the song blends 1950s girl-group melodies with 1960s surf-rock guitar.

lcd soundsystem|dance yrself clean.fact: LCD Soundsystem's "Dance Yrself Clean" opens 2010's This Is Happening with nearly nine minutes of slow build - it starts as a stripped-down, muttering groove before exploding into a full synth-pop eruption around the three-minute mark. Kid Cudi later sampled it for his song "All Talk."

sylvan esso|play it right.fact: Sylvan Esso's "Play It Right" is really the song that created the band - Amelia Meath, then singing in the folk trio Mountain Man, sent her a cappella vocal for the song to electronic producer Nick Sanborn and asked him to rework it his own way. The result was good enough that the two decided to keep making music together as Sylvan Esso.

geese|low era.fact: Geese's "Low Era," from their 2021 debut album Projector, was recorded in drummer Max Bassin's basement, a space the band nicknamed "the Nest" - the band has said four-on-the-floor songs like this one used to feel like poison to them, until they deliberately challenged themselves to write something more danceable.

tv on the radio|province.fact: TV on the Radio's "Province," from 2006's Return to Cookie Mountain, features David Bowie on backing vocals - the album was written by the full band and produced by guitarist Dave Sitek before landing on 4AD.

the decemberists|sucker's prayer.fact: The Decemberists' "Sucker's Prayer," from 2018's I'll Be Your Girl, grew out of Colin Meloy just sitting with a single chord for a while - he's said he had a Karen Dalton song in mind while working it out, and the band had already been playing it live for about a year and a half before they finally recorded it.

car seat headrest|sober to death.fact: Car Seat Headrest's "Sober to Death" is track four on Twin Fantasy - one of only three songs on the album that Will Toledo left lyrically untouched when he re-recorded the whole record from scratch for its 2018 re-release.

primal scream|higher than the sun.fact: Primal Scream's "Higher Than The Sun" comes from 1991's Screamadelica, the album that won the very first Mercury Music Prize in 1992 - house DJs Andrew Weatherall and Terry Farley produced much of it, pushing the band's sound away from straight indie rock into a blend of house, gospel, and dub.

devo|out of sync.fact: DEVO's "Out of Sync," from 1982's Oh, No! It's DEVO, was written by Mark Mothersbaugh and Gerald Casale and built around a riff that nods to The Kinks' "You Really Got Me."

ken park|shatter.fact: Ken Park's "Shatter" is the debut single from Liam Creamer's apartment-recording project - written when he was 17, blending '60s harmonies with '90s indie-rock haze from growing up on My Bloody Valentine, The Smashing Pumpkins, and The Beach Boys' Pet Sounds.

adrianne lenker|anything.fact: Adrianne Lenker's "Anything," from 2020's Songs, reframes love as something familial rather than dramatic - she sings "I don't wanna be the owner of your fantasy, I just wanna be a part of your family," less interested in early-relationship thrills than in just belonging.

kevin morby|pbj.fact: Kevin Morby's "PBJ" reunited him with producer Aaron Dessner of The National, joined by Justin Vernon of Bon Iver on guitar and Andrew Barr on drums. The title comes from a phrase a friend told him - calling driving with the windows down while blasting the AC "Peanut Butter Jelly" - that he's never been able to verify anyone else has heard before.

courtney barnett|one thing at a time.fact: Courtney Barnett's "One Thing At A Time," from 2026's Creature of Habit, was produced by Barnett with John Congleton and Stella Mozgawa - with a bass cameo from the Red Hot Chili Peppers' Flea. Its music video, directed by Lance Bangs, ends with Barnett driving a truck into the Hollywood Hills mid-song.

parquet courts|homosapien.fact: Parquet Courts' "Homosapien" was the final single from 2021's Sympathy for Life - while most of that album grew out of extensive studio jams that got edited and spliced together, "Homosapien" found the band heading back to a more straightforward, guitar-driven garage-rock sound.

ramones|i wanna be sedated.fact: Ramones' "I Wanna Be Sedated," from 1978's Road to Ruin, is Joey Ramone's ode to sheer boredom - inspired partly by a miserable London Christmas stuck in a hotel room with Dee Dee Ramone, and partly by getting burned by hot water and needing hospital treatment. It was also the first song Marky Ramone ever recorded with the band, nailed in just two takes.

ibibio sound machine|concept of love.fact: Ibibio Sound Machine's "Concept of Love" leads their album Chopping Mountain - frontwoman Eno Williams switches between English and Ibibio across the song, an Afro-disco track she's said grew out of wanting to hold onto love, togetherness, and hope amid an unstable world.

bully|days move slow.fact: Bully's "Days Move Slow" was the second single from 2023's Lucky for You, produced by J.T. Daly - it followed "Lose You," a collaboration with fellow Nashville rockers Soccer Mommy, and took about seven months to come together, the longest gestation of any Bully record to that point.

manchester orchestra|simple math.fact: Manchester Orchestra's "Simple Math" is the title track from their 2011 concept album, framed by frontman Andy Hull as "two dueling conversations - me and my wife, and me and my God." It was recorded across multiple studios in Nashville and Atlanta between August and December 2010.

sylvan esso|sledge.fact: Sylvan Esso's "Sledge," from 2026's Ow∞ - their first album on their own label, Psychic Hotline - channels real disasters like Hurricane Helene and the LA wildfires into a tense, three-minute track. Amelia Meath's vocal take was captured almost entirely in first takes, giving it an unpolished immediacy.

bonnie 'prince' billy|a minor place.fact: Bonnie "Prince" Billy's "A Minor Place" opens 1999's I See a Darkness, Will Oldham's first album under that stage name - critics have described its nursery-rhyme-like opening melody as a kind of statement of purpose for the record. The title track later caught Johnny Cash's attention, who recorded his own version of it.

l'rain|5 to 8 hours a day (wwwag).fact: L'Rain's "5 to 8 Hours a Day (WWwaG)," from 2023's I Killed Your Dog, is Taja Cheek's meditation on the discipline artistic work demands - the title nods to the hours-a-day grind of actually making music, folded into her usual blend of R&B, jazz, noise, and pop.

beabadoobee|nothing to prove (feat. hayl.fact: beabadoobee's "Nothing to Prove," featuring Hayley Williams, comes from her 2026 album Pylon - a record whose 14 songs also feature cameos from Turnstile's Brendan Yates and Deftones' Chino Moreno.

andrew bird|eyeoneye.fact: Andrew Bird's "Eyeoneye," the first single from 2012's Break It Yourself, was recorded live in his West Illinois barn straight to 8-track tape with drummer Martin Dosh and guitarist Jeremy Ylvisaker - no studio, no overdubs, just the sound of the room.

cocteau twins|crushed.fact: Cocteau Twins' "Crushed" was made for 4AD's 1987 various-artists compilation Lonely Is an Eyesore - like much of the band's catalog, Elizabeth Fraser's lyrics are deliberately abstract and largely untranslatable, prized more for their sound than any literal meaning.

woods|can't see at all.fact: Woods' "Can't See at All" was one of three singles - along with "Sun City Creeps" and "Morning Light" - that led up to 2016's City Sun Eater in the River of Light, the band's follow-up to 2014's With Light and With Love.

the strokes|reptilia.fact: The Strokes' "Reptilia," the second single from 2003's Room on Fire, gave the album its title - the words "the room is on fire as she's fixing her hair" appear in the song's lyrics. The band scrapped an entire version of the album produced by Radiohead collaborator Nigel Godrich before handing the job back to Is This It producer Gordon Raphael.

destroyer|blue eyes.fact: Destroyer's "Blue Eyes," from 2011's Kaputt, is one of the album's more overtly poetic detours - Dan Bejar repeats the line "I write poetry for myself" over the record's blend of synth-pop, soft rock, and mellow jazz.

amber arcades|something's gonna take you.fact: Amber Arcades is the project of Dutch musician Annelotte de Graaf, whose sound blends folky melodies and spaced-out guitars into what's sometimes called "dreamfolk." "Something's Gonna Take Your Love Away" comes from her 2018 album European Heartbreak.

the decemberists|we both go down togethe.fact: The Decemberists' "We Both Go Down Together" is the second track on 2005's Picaresque - its dramatic string arrangement is carried by violinist Petra Haden, whose playing became one of the album's most talked-about elements.

lala lala|car anymore.fact: Lala Lala's "Car Anymore" opens her 2026 album Heaven 2 with a saxophone cameo from fellow Chicago musician Sen Morimoto.

beach house|pink funeral.fact: Beach House's "Pink Funeral" comes from 2021's Once Twice Melody, the duo's most expansive record - Alex Scally and Victoria Legrand pair a sweeping, string-driven arrangement with one of their darker electronic backdrops, giving the song an almost film-score quality.

alabama shakes|how love s supposed to go.fact: Alabama Shakes' "How Love's Supposed To Go," from 2026's I Must Be Dreaming, opens with a direct hip-hop beat and a heavy bassline hook - the album was produced by the band alongside six-time Grammy winner Shawn Everett.

avalon emerson|jupiter and mars.fact: Avalon Emerson's "Jupiter and Mars" is credited to the full band billing Avalon Emerson & the Charm, released via Dead Oceans in 2026.

waxahatchee|be good.fact: Waxahatchee's "Be Good," from 2017's Out in the Storm, marked a shift away from Katie Crutchfield's earlier lo-fi sound - she recorded it with co-producer John Agnello at Philadelphia's Miner Street Recordings. Her stage name comes from Waxahatchee Creek, near where she grew up in Alabama.

bjork|big time sensuality.fact: Bjork's "Big Time Sensuality," from 1993's Debut, was her breakthrough US hit - she's said the song, despite its title, isn't really about romance: "A lot of my songs...are about my friends, not my lovers. It's not erotic or sensual even if it may sound like that." Its music video has her dancing on the back of a truck driving through New York City.

westside cowboy|paper chains.fact: Westside Cowboy's "Paper Chains" is the second track on 2026's It Goes On, the Manchester four-piece's debut album.

frankie cosmos|abigail.fact: Frankie Cosmos' "Abigail," from 2022's Inner World Peace, is named for a dog Greta Kline became obsessed with years earlier after spotting it on Petfinder - the album art is even her own drawing of a real text conversation about the dog.

sleater-kinney|dig me out.fact: Sleater-Kinney's "Dig Me Out," the title track from their 1997 album, marked the debut of drummer Janet Weiss, who went on to become the band's longest-serving member - guitarist Carrie Brownstein has said the song's riff started life as a nod to Iggy Pop and David Bowie's "China Girl."

fontaines d.c.|marianne.fact: Fontaines D.C.'s "Marianne," the lead single from 2026's Dopamine Chamber, borrows its glamorous, high-stakes aesthetic from Netflix's psychological thriller Ripley - the track was produced by James Ford, and its music video came from director Dave Meyers, known for Kendrick Lamar's "HUMBLE." and Travis Scott's "Sicko Mode."

stereolab|the flower called nowhere.fact: Stereolab's "The Flower Called Nowhere," from 1997's Dots and Loops, was recorded in Dusseldorf with co-production from Andi Toma of Mouse on Mars - part of the album's shift toward denser electronic production, blending bossa nova rhythms with the band's usual avant-pop.

cheekface|plastic.fact: Cheekface's "Plastic" started out as a much bongo-heavier demo before "cooler heads prevailed," according to frontman Greg Katz, who's described the song as being about "being an implacable people pleaser and the miracle of 3D printing."

ebbb|come alive.fact: Ebbb's "Come Alive" opens the British trio's debut album Shallow Hits (2026) - a calypso-tinged burst of electronic pop that blends synth textures with live drumming.

japanese breakfast|kokomo, in.fact: Japanese Breakfast's "Kokomo, IN" comes from 2017's Soft Sounds from Another Planet - Michelle Zauner's acclaimed second album under the Japanese Breakfast name, later re-recorded and included as a bonus cut on 2021's Jubilee.

buzzcocks|what do i get?.fact: Buzzcocks' "What Do I Get?" gave the band their UK chart debut in 1978, peaking at #37 - it followed "Orgasm Addict," their first single, which the BBC refused to play on air. Pete Shelley wrote it and producer Martin Rushent helmed the session.

big thief|shark smile.fact: Big Thief's "Shark Smile," from 2017's Capacity, was recorded in a farmhouse the band was house-sitting at the time - Adrianne Lenker has said she turned her guitar amp all the way up to 10 for the first time while cutting it, inspired by a tour-van diet of Springsteen's Nebraska.

glenn branca|don't let me stop you.fact: Glenn Branca's "Don't Let Me Stop You" is an early recording collected on the 1997 compilation Songs '77-'79 - Branca, credited alongside collaborators from Theoretical Girls and The Static, later became known as an avant-garde composer famous for building symphonies out of massed, alternately-tuned electric guitars.

the war on drugs|holding on.fact: The War on Drugs' "Holding On" led off 2017's A Deeper Understanding, which won the Grammy for Best Rock Album - Adam Granduciel recorded it with engineer Shawn Everett, who's also worked with Alabama Shakes and Weezer, and the song later turned up on the official soundtrack of EA Sports' FIFA 18.

perfume genius|on the floor.fact: Perfume Genius' "On The Floor," from 2020's Set My Heart on Fire Immediately, evokes Eighties R&B by way of Tina Turner and Erasure - the album was produced by Blake Mills with contributions from veteran session players Jim Keltner and Pino Palladino. Mike Hadreas directed the song's music video himself.

2nd grade|anywhere girls.fact: 2nd Grade's "Anywhere Girls" is sung by Catherine Dwyer (also of Remember Sports) rather than the band's usual songwriter, Peter Gill - it comes from Girls and Boys, a 2026 album built as ten songs about girls followed by ten songs about boys.

guv|warmer than gold.fact: GUV's "Warmer Than Gold" is the title track of Ben Cook's 2026 album, made with a wide cast of collaborators including Hatchie and Turnstile's Meg Mills - Cook has said he set out to make a Brit-rock record that sounded like it was produced by the Beastie Boys.

mac demarco|this old dog.fact: Mac DeMarco recorded 2017's This Old Dog using mostly just voice, acoustic guitar, synths, and a drum machine - a deliberately slower, moodier record than his earlier albums, made after he relocated from Queens to Los Angeles and let the songs marinate longer than usual.

songs ohia|blue chicago moon.fact: Songs: Ohia's "Blue Chicago Moon" comes from 2002's Didn't It Rain, an album Jason Molina named after a traditional gospel song popularized by Sister Rosetta Tharpe and Mahalia Jackson - it was recorded by Edan Cohen at Soundgun Studios in Philadelphia.

graham hunt|guardian angel's arms.fact: Graham Hunt's "Guardian Angel's Arms," from 2026's American Pyramid, was recorded with an eight-piece band at Minnesota's Pachyderm Studios - the same studio where Nirvana recorded In Utero.

julian casablancas|11th dimension.fact: Julian Casablancas' "11th Dimension," the lead single from his 2009 solo debut Phrazes for the Young, earned Pitchfork's "Best New Track" honor - Danielle Haim, later of Haim, played drums in the song's music video and in Casablancas' touring band.

interpol|wings on fire.fact: Interpol debuted "Wings On Fire" live in Albuquerque in April 2026, ahead of its release on This Mirror Weighs a Ton - their first album since 2022's The Other Side of Make-Believe.

wilco|locator.fact: Wilco's "Locator" was released as the lead single from 2016's Schmilco - the band put it out on the exact one-year anniversary of their surprise previous album, also called Star Wars. Where Star Wars leaned into fuzzy glam guitars, Schmilco was a much more acoustic, stripped-down record.

spoon|the ghost of you lingers.fact: Spoon's "The Ghost of You Lingers," from 2007's Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga, leans into a Spaghetti Western sound - critics have compared its dramatic sweep to a Morricone score wrapped in lo-fi garage-rock grit.

ty segall|hospital.fact: Ty Segall's "Hospital" opens his 2026 album Chrome - released the same day as a companion EP, Love Fuzzz, both recorded with his full band of Ben Boye, Evan Burrows, Mikal Cronin, and Emmett Kelly.

depeche mode|black celebration.fact: Depeche Mode's title track "Black Celebration" opens their 1986 album of the same name - the band built its unique sound entirely from their own samples rather than outside sources, and at one point considered sampling a Winston Churchill speech before scrapping the idea. Engineers later said they could barely remember how they'd made some of the sounds when they went back to remaster it in 2006.

sonic youth|the sprawl.fact: Sonic Youth's "The Sprawl," from 1988's Daydream Nation, takes its title from the sprawling fictional megacity - stretching from Boston to Atlanta - in William Gibson's cyberpunk novels. The album was the band's first double LP and their last for an independent label before signing to Geffen.

kurt vile|one trick ponies.fact: Kurt Vile's "One Trick Ponies," from 2018's Bottle It In, opens with an egg shaker, a countdown, and Vile blurting "ohhh, shit" once the beat kicks in - Barack Obama later named it one of his favorite songs of the year.

foals|olympic airways.fact: Foals' "Olympic Airways," the fourth and final single from 2008's Antidotes, is about the pull of wanting to stay home rather than go out into the world, according to frontman Yannis Philippakis - it later turned up on the FIFA 09 soundtrack and on a Forza Horizon game's in-game Sub Pop Records radio station.

the national|light years.fact: The National's "Light Years" closes out 2019's I Am Easy to Find, an album recorded at their Long Pond studio in the Hudson Valley with sessions also in Paris, Berlin, Cincinnati, Austin, Dublin, and Brooklyn - it features guest vocals across the record from Sharon Van Etten, Lisa Hannigan, Mina Tindle, and the Brooklyn Youth Chorus.

slow pulp|spill.fact: Slow Pulp's "Spill" was actually the first song written for 2023's Yard - but it didn't click until producer Elliot Kozel got involved years later, and it ended up finding its home instead on 2026's Melodie.

iron & wine|me and lazarus.fact: Iron & Wine's "Me and Lazarus," from 2013's Ghost on Ghost, was recorded in New York with a cast of jazz and Americana players - including Bob Dylan bassist Tony Garnier, jazz drummer Brian Blade, and members of Antony and the Johnsons - all brought together by producer Brian Deck.

fiona apple|cosmonauts.fact: Fiona Apple wrote "Cosmonauts" for Judd Apatow's 2012 film This Is 40, recording it first with Jon Brion, who ultimately didn't use it in the movie - she later re-recorded it for her own album instead. Apatow had asked for a song about two people staying together forever, which Apple found a strange assignment since she wasn't sure she believed in that herself.

radiohead|black star.fact: Radiohead's "Black Star" came out of an unplanned session during the making of The Bends - producer John Leckie stepped out one day, and engineer Nigel Godrich stayed behind with the band to record it, in what became his first work with Radiohead. Godrich has produced every Radiohead album since.

ian sweet|criminal kissing.fact: IAN SWEET's "Criminal Kissing" comes from Shiverstruck, an album produced by Ben H. Allen (Animal Collective, Soccer Mommy) at Maze Studios in Atlanta - the record arrived roughly a decade after Jilian Medford released her debut IAN SWEET album, Shapeshifter.
